provinces.name: Ontario
provinces.analysis:
Ontario's unemployment rate held at 7.6% in the February Labour Force Survey, +0.3 percentage points from the prior month and the highest provincial print in Central Canada1. The participation rate rose +0.2 percentage points to 64.6% while the employment rate held flat at 59.7%, below the national 60.6% figure1. The provincial CPI series printed at -1.1% year-over-year, the lowest provincial CPI reading in the country2. Housing starts came in at 67,274 units (CMHC seasonally adjusted annualized), up from 65,757 the prior month3.

Finance Minister Peter Bethlenfalvy tabled the Ontario Budget 2026 on March 26, raising the ten-year capital plan to over $210 billion, with $37 billion for 2026-27 and approximately $64 billion over ten years for health infrastructure including ~50 hospital projects and ~3,000 new beds4. The budget added $300 million to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund and confirmed $31 billion over ten years for highway investment, with work underway on Highway 413, the Bradford Bypass, the Highway 7 expansion between Kitchener and Guelph, the Garden City Skyway twinning, and Highway 401 upgrades5. The project database tracks 647 Ontario projects valued at $254.4B, of which 234 are Under Construction, 153 Proposed, 94 Approved, and 30 Under Review; infrastructure (198), healthcare (134), and transit and rail (128) are the largest sector categories6.

The Adaptive Phased Management Deep Geological Repository ($26.0B, Proposed, Nuclear Waste Management Organization) remains in the federal Impact Assessment Registry, alongside the Ontario Line ($27.4B, Under Construction) and GO Expansion ($26.1B, Under Construction) as the province's largest active capital files7. Ontario building permits stood at $2,690.8M in the latest StatCan print9. The Bank of Canada delivers its next interest rate decision on April 16, which is tracked alongside Ontario's rate-sensitive residential and infrastructure pipeline8.

provinces.name: Quebec
provinces.analysis:
Quebec's unemployment rate printed at 5.9% in the February Labour Force Survey, +0.7 percentage points from the prior 5.2% reading; the participation rate fell -0.3 percentage points to 64.5% and the employment rate fell -0.8 percentage points to 60.7%1. The provincial CPI series printed at +0.6% year-over-year, below the national signal2. Housing starts came in at 53,461 units in the latest CMHC release, up from 51,982 the prior month3. Quebec carries the richest provincial indicator library after the national rollup, with Institut de la statistique du Québec series running parallel to StatCan prints2.

The Quebec Treasury Board tabled the Plan québécois des infrastructures 2026-2036 on March 18, totalling $167 billion over ten years with $12.6 billion in new funding for health and social services, education, higher education, and public transit4. The transport investment plan separately allocates $8 billion for road, marine, rail, and airport infrastructure across 2026-20288. Bill 5, advanced through the National Assembly in March, creates a fast-track regulatory pathway for 'priority national-scale projects' assessed on prosperity, autonomy, Indigenous consultation, energy-transition targets, and short-term implementability criteria5. The project database tracks 490 Quebec projects valued at $89.3B, of which 281 are Approved, 86 Under Review, 83 Proposed, and 39 Under Construction6. Education (118), infrastructure (103), and healthcare (49) are the largest sector categories.

Anchor capital files include the Parc éolien zone Chamouchouane ($9.0B, Proposed, Hydro-Québec/MRC Domaine du Roy), the Quebec Transport Infrastructure Investment Plan ($8.0B, Proposed), the revised Montreal Metro Blue Line Extension ($4.89B, Under Construction, STM), the TES Canada green hydrogen facility at Shawinigan ($4.0B, Under Review), and the Québec City Tramway TramCité project ($3.76B, Under Construction)7.

provinces.name: Alberta
provinces.analysis:
Alberta's unemployment rate printed at 6.3% in the February Labour Force Survey, -0.1 percentage points from January, while the participation rate fell -0.3 percentage points to 68.7% and the employment rate fell -0.1 percentage points to 64.4%1. Alberta's participation rate remains the highest in the country, consistent with sustained resource-sector labour demand. The provincial CPI series printed at +3.4% year-over-year, the highest provincial CPI reading in Canada2. Housing starts came in at 48,438 units in the latest CMHC release, down from 48,896 the prior month3. Provincial GDP printed at +2.7%.

The Federal-Alberta-Pathways Alliance tri-lateral Memorandum of Understanding targeted April 1 for a multi-phased framework on the proposed $16.5 billion carbon capture and storage trunkline in northern Alberta, covering carbon-price alignment and CCS financing4. The Pathways Alliance rebranded to the 'Oil Sands Alliance' in February5. The Pathways Alliance CO2 Transportation Network and Storage Hub Project (IAAC Registry entry 89090) is currently in planning phase7. The project database tracks 724 Alberta projects valued at $349.6B — the second-largest provincial pipeline by total value — with 384 Proposed, 172 Under Construction, 83 Complete, 63 Under Review, and 20 Approved; government (146), power and energy (124), and infrastructure (113) are the largest sector categories6.

Anchor capital files include the Alberta Budget 2026 Capital Plan ($28.3B, Proposed)8, the Telus Infrastructure Upgrades province-wide 2023-2027 ($19.0B, Under Construction), the Pathways Alliance CCS Hub Phase 1 ($16.5B, Proposed), and AOSP Jackpine ($12.0B, Approved, Canadian Natural Resources Limited)67. The Bank of Canada delivers its next rate decision on April 16, which is tracked alongside the energy sector's capex sensitivity9.

provinces.name: British Columbia
provinces.analysis:
British Columbia's unemployment rate held at 6.1% in the February Labour Force Survey, flat from January, while the participation rate fell -0.4 percentage points to 64.4% and the employment rate fell -0.4 percentage points to 60.5%1. The provincial CPI series printed at +1.0% year-over-year, below the national signal2. Housing starts came in at 41,331 units in the latest CMHC release, down marginally from 41,492 the prior month3. Provincial GDP printed at +1.2%.

BC filed three policy items this week — a March housing highlights statement, a reaction to the U.S. Department of Commerce preliminary softwood lumber duty determination, and an April rental report statement — all under Ministers Boyle (Housing) and Parmar (Forests)45. The U.S. preliminary duty rate came in at just under 25%, below the current ~35% combined rate; the BC Forests Ministry characterized the U.S. process as broken5. Two new rental buildings opened in West Vancouver under the housing accelerator framework7. The project database tracks 648 British Columbia projects valued at $509.6B — the largest provincial pipeline in Canada — with 251 Proposed, 153 Under Construction, 120 Under Review, 42 Approved, and 29 On Hold6. Power and energy (68), mining (56), and the 'Other' category (60) lead by sector count.

Anchor capital files include LNG Canada Phase 1 ($47.9B, Under Construction, Shell/Petronas/PetroChina/Mitsubishi/Korea Gas), the LNG Canada Facility ($40.0B, Complete), LNG Canada Phase 2 ($25.0B, Proposed — no FID), Kitimat Clean Oil Refinery ($22.0B, Under Review), and the Peace River Site C Hydro-electric project ($16.0B, Under Construction)10. Woodfibre LNG at Squamish has marine pile works underway under BC Energy Regulator oversight8. The Bank of Canada delivers its next rate decision on April 16, which is tracked alongside the BC residential and LNG capex pipeline9.

provinces.name: Saskatchewan
provinces.analysis:
Saskatchewan's unemployment rate printed at 5.6% in the February Labour Force Survey, +0.3 percentage points from the prior 5.3% reading; the participation rate fell -0.5 percentage points to 67.1% and the employment rate fell -0.6 percentage points to 63.4%1. Saskatchewan's unemployment rate sits among the lowest provincial prints in Canada, tied with Quebec's ISQ reading. The provincial CPI series printed at -0.7% year-over-year2, and provincial GDP printed at +3.4%. Housing starts came in at 5,486 units in the latest CMHC release, up from 5,327 the prior month3.

BHP's Jansen potash mine is now 75% complete; Stage 1 first production has slipped to 2027 (a one-year delay) and Stage 2 has slipped to 2031 (a two-year delay)45. Stage 1 capex is up approximately 30% from the original plan, and total BHP capital in Jansen now stands at approximately C$14 billion57. Nutrien remains the largest Saskatchewan producer at 20 megatonnes per year across six mines4. The project database tracks 213 Saskatchewan projects valued at $38.3B, of which 90 are Proposed, 78 Under Review, 34 Under Construction, and 10 Approved6.

Anchor capital files include Jansen Stage 1 ($7.5B, Under Construction, BHP), Jansen Stage 2 ($6.4B, Under Construction, BHP), the Saskatchewan 2026-27 Capital Budget ($4.3B, Approved), the Federated Co-operatives Limited HDRD Plant in Regina ($2.0B, Proposed), and the Bell Canada AI Data Centre at the RM of Sherwood ($1.7B, Proposed) — a 300 MW facility announced as part of Bell's national AI fabric expansion68.

provinces.name: Manitoba
provinces.analysis:
Manitoba's unemployment rate printed at 5.7% in the February Labour Force Survey, -0.6 percentage points from the prior 6.3% reading; the participation rate fell -0.8 percentage points to 66.3% and the employment rate fell -0.4 percentage points to 62.5%1. Manitoba's employment rate remains above the national 60.6% figure. The provincial CPI series printed at +3.1% year-over-year2, and provincial GDP printed at +1.1%. Housing starts came in at 7,642 units in the latest CMHC release, down from 7,799 the prior month3.

The Kinew government tabled Manitoba Budget 2026 on March 24, projecting a $1.7 billion deficit in 2025-26 falling to $498 million in 2026-27 and an $8 million surplus in 2027-2848. Strategic infrastructure spending was set at $3.7 billion for the fiscal year, an average of approximately $4.3 billion per year over five years4. Manitoba Hydro received $1.17 billion in capital investment under the budget, while Hydro itself is forecasting a $502 million net loss — a $722 million swing from a prior $220 million net income projection — attributed to water conditions48. The project database tracks 2,058 Manitoba projects valued at $14.6B, with the count inflated by 1,976 Under Review filings from the Manitoba Environmental Licensing registry; 42 are Under Construction, 31 Proposed, and 9 Approved6.

Anchor capital files include the Manitoba Budget 2026 line item ($3.8B, Proposed), the North End Water Pollution Control Centre Upgrade ($3.2B, Under Construction) which hit a UV milestone this quarter, the Portage Place Redevelopment Healthcare Centre of Excellence ($650M, Under Construction), the NEWPCC Biosolids Facility ($502M, Approved), and the Lake Manitoba/Lake St. Martin Outlet Channels Project ($495M, Approved)57.

provinces.analysis:

provinces.name: Prince Edward Island
provinces.analysis:
Prince Edward Island's unemployment rate printed at 7.2% in the February Labour Force Survey, -0.4 percentage points from the prior 7.6% reading; the participation rate rose +0.1 percentage points to 66.6% and the employment rate rose +0.3 percentage points to 61.8%1. The provincial CPI series printed at +5.4% year-over-year — the highest provincial CPI reading in Canada2 — and provincial GDP printed at +3.6%. Housing starts came in at 963 units in the latest CMHC release, down from 1,112 the prior month3.

PEI's 2026-2027 Operating Budget remains in pre-budget consultation; the province has reported population +1.6% to 182,657 through July 2025, employment +1.2% through October 2025, and international exports +12.8% through August 20254. The Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program has approved more than $21.7 million across three PEI projects; the province launched a $10 million cleantech R&D fund and three tax-free development zones4. The Eastern Kings Wind Farm Expansion (+29.4 MW, seven turbines) remains in commissioning, and PEI's wind share of provincial generation reached 98.2% in 2023, the highest in Canada4. The project database tracks 96 PEI projects valued at $2.9B, of which 74 are Under Construction, 14 Proposed, 5 Approved, and 3 Under Review6.

Anchor capital files include the PEI 2026-27 Capital Budget healthcare and education infrastructure line ($486M, Proposed)5, the PEI Capital Budget 2026-27 five-year plan ($1.6B) covering the new hospital and schools8, the PEI Mental Health Campus Completion ($131M, Under Construction), affordable housing construction of 300+ units ($100M, Proposed), and the Northumberland Strait Submarine Transmission System ($92M, Under Construction)7.
